### New files

**`packages/api-client/src/v2/blocks/response-block/helpers/resolve-response-content-type.ts`**
- `DEFAULT_RESPONSE_CONTENT_TYPE = 'text/plain;charset=UTF-8'`
- `resolveResponseContentType(contentType)` — returns the input unchanged when it's a non-null string, else the default.
- `resolveResponseMimeType(contentType)` — parses to a MIME object; `essence` defaults to `'text/plain'` for null/undefined.

**`packages/api-client/src/v2/blocks/response-block/helpers/resolve-response-body-handler.ts`**
- `resolveResponseBodyHandler(mimeType, plugins)` — normalizes the MIME type to its essence, then returns the first handler with a case-insensitive, wildcard-glob-matching pattern (e.g. `application/vnd.*+json`). Skips plugins without `responseBody`.

### Modified files

**`packages/oas-utils/src/helpers/client-plugins.ts`** (+ `index.ts`) — added the `ResponseBodyHandler` type (`mimeTypes`, optional `decode(buf, contentType?)`, optional `language`), added optional `responseBody` to `ClientPlugin`, and exported the type. Rebuilt the `oas-utils` dist so downstream type-checking sees the new type.

**`decode-buffer.ts`** — now `async`, accepts an optional `pluginHandler?: ResponseBodyHandler`. When the handler has a `decode`, it calls `handler.decode(buffer, contentType)` (awaiting sync/async results); otherwise falls back to default text/binary decoding.

**`send-request.ts`** — argument object now accepts `plugins`. In the standard-response path it resolves the content type (falling back to the default when the header is missing), resolves a plugin handler against that resolved type, and awaits `decodeBuffer(...)` with it.

**`process-response-body.ts`** — uses `resolveResponseMimeType`, so `mimeType.essence` defaults to `'text/plain'` when no content-type header is present.
